text:
## Creative brief
1) 1 minute video about Competitive runner named Jason talks about his family's background and his Jewish heritage -- how his grandpa came to New York, and what running means to him in the context of his family history.

2) One camera interview (two files, about 15 minutes total) and several b-roll clips. A few music options and light flares.

3) - Start with Jason introducing himself and how his family came to America. - Open with the drone shot overhead. - Make the b-roll black and white and 'old footage' style, like it is archival. - Use the piano track that has a more old-fashioned feel. - Make the mix of interview to b-roll 75% interview to 25% b-roll.

## Overview & Tone

This 60-second piece is an intimate, heritage-driven portrait of Jason Deck, balancing personal family history with athletic purpose. To satisfy the 75/25 interview-to-b-roll ratio while creating a reverent, generational feel, the visual language separates present-day reality from ancestral memory: Jason’s on-camera dialogue remains warm, natural, and front-and-center in a tight 9:16 vertical crop, while the cutaways are treated with high-contrast monochrome, subtle film grain, and organic optical flares to feel like recovered archival film. An understated, vintage piano cue anchors the pacing, giving Jason’s reflections room to breathe without sentimentality.

## Story Beats

#### 1. Introduction & Immigration Roots (0:00–0:24) [node: beat_95b230ad-8389-41a4-9ffc-eb621e54498a]

We open cold on visual texture before seeing Jason's face. Under soft city ambiance, the contemplative piano theme [node: card_e098f554-23fe-43ff-a785-5bb20a4fd73a] eases in as we roll the overhead drone shot grouped with street light flare and projector audio [node: card_4e0b0b47-f8f8-4608-bb8e-b0a6160dfea8] (Lens_Flare_From_The_Street_Light_fhd_1184157 (0s–10s); DJI_20260503181611_0001_D (43s–63s)). As planned in [node: card_42c09118-f5ed-49cb-bead-56ca1db4ece6], the drone shot is reframed vertically and graded in grainy, high-contrast black-and-white. Over this 4-second visual prologue, we hear Jason’s voiceover introduction [node: card_f9ea8a3d-db2b-4b93-80c8-d703cc0cb480] pulled from P1071636-003 [node: card_8002d495-82c4-4c68-944a-f7153202fe83] (P1071636-003 (114.81s–119.07s)), which grounds his identity in Brooklyn and Nice Jewish Runners.

At 0:04, we cut directly on-camera to Jason's interview from P1071637-002 [node: card_081900bb-9475-45b1-b339-3373c0c62865] (P1071637-002 (27.61s–50.29s)), framed in an intimate vertical medium close-up as he delivers his reflection on the bridge between the old world and the new world [node: card_fd2b215f-b420-4253-a60e-0da15ed4c2c7]. We hold on Jason uninterrupted through his mention of his grandfather arriving in Washington Heights in the late 1940s and competing for Maccabi New York, establishing the emotional stakes through his face and voice rather than masking it with unnecessary cutaways.

#### 2. The Grandfather's New York Legacy (0:24–0:37) [node: beat_2eacfb68-cf64-4f1b-bed0-2e9d5e258d0d]

As Jason broadens the ancestral lineage to Holocaust survivors and Ellis Island migrations [node: card_159fa454-f7f2-4772-a0e9-8c49ee6cef40], we transition directly into P1071638 [node: card_9a36e895-78de-4cbf-aac5-aeda55c643e0] (P1071638 (26.07s–36.97s)). The reflective piano score swells slightly beneath his voice [node: card_db3aa5f4-5e64-4846-b965-acaeb2311e81], deepening the emotional resonance. 

To honor the 75% interview rule while adding kinetic energy, we hold on Jason’s face for the setup, then cut away for a brief 3-second burst of stylized monochrome b-roll showing running shoes rhythmically striking the pavement [node: card_cd86d74c-8fcb-458e-a608-4266c349fbfb] (P1071661 (0s–3.5s)), executed according to the cutaway rhythm outlined in [node: card_21e84a51-54a6-4363-a3bf-f877bd4010f7]. The alternative track jog shot P1071648 [node: card_d93b47f8-3ff8-4095-95ae-8d06afd18366] (P1071648 (5s–10s)) is intentionally omitted here; stacking multiple wide running clips would dilute the intimacy of the survivor narrative and tip the runtime past the target 25% b-roll threshold. We cut straight back to Jason on-camera as he finishes the thought.

#### 3. Coming Full Circle (0:37–0:50) [node: beat_6381a8b4-7392-404c-ae07-12fc7394a978]

We pivot cleanly from the historical past to Jason’s personal pride in the present using interview take P1071636-003 [node: card_157e0c85-0cc8-49e6-b531-aea22a7efd4e] (P1071636-003 (475.12s–499.26s)), where he speaks about wearing his team jersey publicly and sharing those photos with his grandfather [node: card_4ab7a2d1-593c-4f1f-b992-bc9c8fcd8307]. The piano continues beneath the speech with steady emotional momentum [node: card_0d829f6c-32f5-4fb9-ac03-134cd16494aa].

To emphasize the generational connection, we follow the editorial intent in [node: card_3c281497-72dd-450d-8d5a-8555a41da067] by inserting a 4-second stylized b-roll cutaway to the Star of David embroidery on his jacket [node: card_5c3c6840-c3fb-4d46-958f-02959e314df6] (P1071659 (13s–29s)), treated with the same archival black-and-white grade. We leave out the bench clip of tying shoes from P1071640 [node: card_d375f152-706e-441f-8bc8-a4e131fdc0cd] (P1071640 (0s–5s)), as the jacket emblem directly symbolizes the "Nice Jewish Runners" jersey Jason is speaking about, creating a tight visual-verbal match without cluttering the edit.

#### 4. Identity & Running with Pride (0:50–1:00) [node: beat_2cdbd8d4-2fe6-4ce2-a610-228edb089e64]

For the final sequence, we cut back to Jason on-camera from P1071638 [node: card_61d68461-56c5-4f5e-84b8-681c42c8c4d6] (P1071638 (43.27s–59.43s)) as he delivers his closing synthesis: that this lineage is the American Jewish story, and that running with his club exemplifies that pride [node: card_8a9a1123-3bc8-48a5-8e5d-5e43897f13b6]. 

Just as his closing line finishes, we cut away for the final 4 seconds per [node: card_014489c5-2f2b-4916-aa1e-d09e2adf971f] to the monochrome archival shot of Jason on the track breaking into an authentic, warm smile [node: card_4f0e4d91-55d6-4084-89b4-17923b845850] (P1071658 (1s–6s)). The piano hits its resolving final chord and sustains into room tone [node: card_1972d384-00fb-4683-bb43-23b7ec650053], lingering on his smile before fading gently to black at exactly the 60-second mark.

## Constraints

- The plan above is the spec — it already made the editorial calls (what to use, what to omit, how to sequence and combine material). Follow the plan's own decisions rather than independently re-deriving them from first principles.
- Track is authoritative for whatever the plan places on a given track. A shot the plan describes as A-Roll must land on the A-Roll track, B-Roll on B-Roll, music on the Music track, and text/graphics on the Text/Graphics track. A card does not count as fulfilled merely because related material appears elsewhere in the timeline on the wrong track.
- Timecodes and durations in the plan are approximate targets, not exact requirements — use editorial judgment on the actual cut points, same as any real edit.
- A Music card whose source names a real file path (marked "real stock audio file") must be added directly with `edit-timeline add-clip <path> --row music --role music` — do not call `/generate music` for it.

## Instructions for tagging

When adding a clip with `edit-timeline add-clip`, attach the corresponding plan node ID using `--node-ids card_<id>` (or `beat_<id>` for a beat-level marker).

If one clip fulfills multiple plan node ids, include all applicable ones.

Only attach a node ID when the clip actually fulfills what the plan describes for it, including its named track. Use the exact node IDs from the plan. Do not invent or modify them.

## Completion requirements

Before finishing, verify against the plan's own decisions, not the original grid.

For each beat, confirm the edit the plan describes was actually realized: the right material landed on the right track, in the intended order, with any transitions/overlaps the plan called out.

For any node id the plan itself named as an intentionally unused alternative or backup, no further action is needed — that was already the plan's own decision, not something to silently reconsider or silently include anyway.

A node id that the plan actively describes using, but that never lands on the corresponding clip, is a real gap — note it and the reason in verification.
